correctness.rationale: For the unit-edge cube, the Lipschitz seminorm equals twice the maximum coordinate half-difference norm. Differentiation commutes with Walsh spectral projection after deleting that frequency coordinate; the resulting Walsh convolution has exact \(L_\infty\) operator norm equal to the mean absolute coordinate-shadow kernel. The explicitly defined globally compatible Boolean sign-gradient witness has seminorm two and attains each coordinate-shadow kernel norm, proving equality. Pointed translations are isometries diagonalizing every anchored Walsh character; averaging any projection onto a selected family gives the unique equivariant projection, proving minimality in both the Lipschitz space and finite dual free space. The Krawtchouk count and degree-two binomial identity are algebraically derived. A self-contained integer/rational checker passed 585 nonempty spectrum witness checks and 23 quadratic moment identities; an additional independent LP implementation of finite norm constraints matched 158 instances. These experiments are supplemental rather than proofs of infinite families.

originality.rationale: The exact sup-norm Walsh kernel identity and Krawtchouk asymptotics were previously published. A quantitative transfer to the Lipschitz seminorm, with a compatible sign-gradient extremizer for every coordinate-shadow, and minimum projection norms on both Lipschitz and Lipschitz-free spaces was not found in the compared full texts. The 2021 norm-one group-orbit projections do not imply general spectral projection constants. value.rationale: The theorem computes the exact relative projection constant simultaneously for every nonempty Walsh spectral family on each unweighted finite Hamming cube, on both the Lipschitz and its free-space sides, reducing a coupled gradient optimization to n explicit lower-dimensional Walsh-kernel first moments. A single natural family of quadratic layers gives sharp unbounded \(\sqrt n\) behavior despite rank-one character projections being contractive, an informative structural contrast for complemented finite Fourier decompositions. These are natural operator invariants; the motivation lies in the geometry of Lipschitz-free spaces and discrete Fourier truncations, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
